name: Baingan Bharta
ingredients: 1 large (500g) purple eggplant (brinjal), preferably long and firm
2 green bird's eye chilies, slit (adjust to heat preference)
1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder (or mild paprika for color)
1 tablespoon homemade garam masala (clove, cinnamon, cardamom, black pepper)
3 tablespoons mustard oil (or ghee for a nuttier flavor)
A handful of fresh coriander leaves, chopped
Optional: 1 teaspoon amchur (dry mango powder) for tang
instructions: 1. Roast the eggplant directly over a gas flame or charcoal grill, turning frequently until the skin is completely charred and the flesh feels soft. (Alternatively, broil in oven at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, turning once.)
2. Let the eggplant cool, then peel off the charred skin. Gently mash the flesh with a fork; keep some coarse bits for texture. Set aside.
3. Heat mustard oil in a heavy kadhai or pan until it smokes lightly. Add cumin seeds; they should sizzle immediately.
4. Add chopped onions and cook on medium-high heat until deep golden brown, about 8-10 minutes, scraping the pan to incorporate caramelized bits.

5. Stir in ginger, garlic, and green chilies; cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add diced tomatoes, turmeric, and red chili powder. Cook until tomatoes break down and oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
6. Lower heat; add the mashed eggplant, garam masala, and salt. Mix well and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing flavors to meld.
7. (Optional) Add amchur for extra tang. Taste and adjust salt. Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve hot with warm tandoori roti or paratha.
description: A smoky, soulful symphony of fire-roasted eggplant, caramelized onions, and fragrant spices, embodying the rustic heart of Punjab.
